# Explain contributor assistance and the choice to request help

Pickup is held for the shared workflow alignment described below.

## Context

D#21005 ratifies contributor-chosen assistance, with [current bound approval](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21005#discussioncomment-19632510). neomjs/neo-agent-skills#399 owns the maintainer policy; neomjs/neo-agent-skills#398 owns its outcome. This leaf gives Engine contributors the corresponding public choice in the two entry surfaces below. The [November 19 Engine agreement](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21367#issuecomment-7021637790) distinguishes first-time and returning contributor reviews. [The shared workflow](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/blob/dev/.agents/skills/pull-request/references/pull-request-workflow.md) still requires affirmative consent for the first content push on every PR. Reconcile that wording in the shared policy before contributor pickup, then satisfy the parent’s Engine activation gates before rollout.

## The Problem / Architectural Reality

The contribution guide and PR template are the contributor-facing inputs; internal skills alone cannot tell an author what help means. The existing Engine guide distinguishes claim-before-work, one issue per PR and dev as target. Those rules must stay coherent while assistance is explained.

Design authority: "An unchecked optional checkbox invites an offer." — [D#21005, accepted candidate 13:57:26Z](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21005#discussioncomment-19632343).

## The Fix / Contract Ledger

| Surface | Required behaviour | Fallback / edge | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CONTRIBUTING: returning contributors | Correct PRs can be approved. For requested changes, use one complete actionable review and an author-led meaningful revision unless help is requested sooner. The first maintainer content push needs the author’s affirmative reply accepting its scope. Later changes stay inside it. | A contributor can decline or withdraw help. New behavior, API or design choices, substantial replacements and meaningful conflict resolutions need new agreement. | A returning contributor can identify their next action and what an affirmative reply authorizes. |
| CONTRIBUTING: first-time contributors | Under the November 19 Engine agreement, a maintainer can finish settled review items on the original PR for a good-faith contributor with no prior merged organization PRs, using an authorized branch route and preserving the original contributor’s work, PR body and credit. Use independent approval of the resulting head. | The agreement covers settled review items. Ask the contributor for decisions about their intent if needed. Missing branch permission routes to a maintainer with the required access. An approval-worthy draft can be marked ready without asking, since that changes no content. | Walk a first PR through a bounded review repair, an intent decision, and independent approval. |
| PR template | An **unchecked, optional invitation** to offer help, clearly distinguished from authorization. Preserve existing issue, dev-target, change-kind and disclosure requirements. CLI/agent users learn the same choice from the guide. | A checked or auto-filled box never substitutes for the scoped reply; no mandatory checkbox or rejection for leaving it blank. | Inspect both initial checked/unchecked examples; no new runtime test needed. |
| Integration handback | Maintainers own base-move integration through remote head verification, CI and current-head approval for first-time contributors. For returning contributors, handle mechanical base churn where an authorized route works, with at most one contributor rebase request caused by our moving base. Merge the base while preserving contributor commits. After a maintainer update, use `git pull --ff-only` on the correctly tracking branch. | If the pull refuses on local divergence, preserve work and ask for assisted reconciliation. Keep the Git work with a capable maintainer when the only question for the author is intent. | Plain-language examples of both handback paths and what to do if a local branch diverges. |
| Time / credit / residual | Dependency dates name an available next action, exact date/timezone and at least three working days from the latest legitimate action-adding handback. Our waits do not count. Ordinary check-ins and existing claim expiry are distinct. Keep original PR merge credit; retarget a useful residual if its original issue already merged. | No automatic takeover or date reset; a declined offer does not itself justify replacement. Separate continuation credits retained work without inventing the original author’s merge count. | Reader walk for absent consent, return date, our CI wait, release/recommitment and already-merged target. |
| Scope of the public promise | Explain the contributor’s choices and next step. Maintainer execution, independent approval and rollout gates stay with neomjs/neo-agent-skills#398, neomjs/neo-agent-skills#399 and the Brain/program leaves. | Do not burden contributors with private Task access, internal gate checklists or claims that automatic rerouting is already delivered. | Source/activation status is explicit in the PR handoff and owning rollout record. |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Guide and template implement both review paths in the ledger, with no new badge rung, claim limit/expiry, competence threshold or repeated-rebase obligation.
- [ ] The invitation’s unchecked default and non-authorizing meaning are explicit. An independent read using only these entry surfaces correctly identifies consent, next owner, safe local-branch handback and credit.
- [ ] An already-merged target with useful residual is handled by proposed retargeting on the original PR before replacement; the reader understands that content scope still needs agreement.
- [ ] Existing close-target/dev/disclosure conventions and links remain valid; run the repository’s applicable link checks. Do not add mirror tests for prose.
- [ ] Record the exact source revision and coordinate the dated Engine activation with the parent. Source merge alone is not proof of loaded policy, runtime independence or routed-seat capability.

## Binding slice

## Out of Scope / Avoided Traps

No claim-responder implementation or issue-body backfill (Mnemosyne’s neomjs/neo#20892 stream), sibling rollout, permission settings, badge calculation or review-predicate code. Keep the public entry useful to a person; keep record-wire mechanics in their owning maintainer contract.

unowned-rationale: Pickup is held while the shared workflow still uses the November 15 consent rule for all contributors. The [alignment finding](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21025#issuecomment-7026726574) and [November 19 Engine agreement](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21367#issuecomment-7021637790) define the correction. The [initial policy publication](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/issues/401#issuecomment-6900766523) and [shared Engine template](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21056) are available for implementation after the shared rule is reconciled. Sophie owns the alignment and eventual review handoff. Keep this leaf unassigned for a contributor when that blocker clears. The parent’s activation conditions still apply.

`[ARCH_ALIGNMENT]` **Short-horizon currency check (`ticket-intake` §1.7.5 / `successor-risk-audit.md §1.1`) — hold pickup pending 19 Nov first-timer carve-out alignment:**

During intake review at `dev` `2e594a683b`, two post-filing developments reshape Row 1 (*CONTRIBUTING: review and help*) and Row 3 (*Integration handback*) of the Nov 15 Contract Ledger above:

1. **Operator ruling on first-time vs. returning contributors (`2026-11-19`, recorded on `#21367` [`#issuecomment-7021637790`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21367#issuecomment-7021637790) and Memory Core `00baed99-ff98-4e9b-a8c1-1a697b35cacd`):**
   - For **first-time contributors** (`0` prior merged org PRs + good-faith check), maintainers finish review items directly on the PR branch (merge `dev` in without rebasing contributor commits, leave the PR body untouched, coordinate via A2A) without asking the contributor first, so newcomers do not stall or get confused by round-trip ceremonies.
   - **Returning contributors** use the normal time-boxed review and scoped-consent loop.
   - Row 1 of this ticket's Nov 15 ledger currently prescribes the opposite for first PRs (*"otherwise one complete actionable review, then an author-led meaningful revision unless help requested sooner... the first content push needs the author's affirmative reply accepting the named scope... No competence/consent inference from labels or merge counts"*).
2. **Draft-PR ready-flip & newcomer base-conflict ownership (`skills#398` [`#issuecomment-6923490857`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/issues/398#issuecomment-6923490857) & [`#issuecomment-6965421314`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/issues/398#issuecomment-6965421314)):**
   - Maintainers own base-move conflict integration end-to-end for newcomers (`merge`-method `gh pr update-branch`) and mark approval-worthy draft PRs ready (`gh pr ready`) without waiting on an author reply.

Leaving `#21025` unassigned for now rather than publishing Nov 15 wording into `CONTRIBUTING.md` that contradicts the 19 Nov first-timer rule; cc `@neo-gpt-sophie` and `@neo-opus-vega` so `pull-request-workflow.md` §10 and this ledger stay in lockstep before contributor/maintainer pickup.
